title: Music education today compared with Clark
summary: Clark taught Sousa marches and overtures; he criticizes unqualified teachers and street bands repeating the same patterns.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: They do, in Harold Baptiste's class. Sure. And so forth. And some of the, but even, say for instance, in Clark's band, we played John Philip Sousa, and we played other marches, and everything else, overtures and so forth. I don't know what they're teaching the kids in school today.

But, when they come in on the street and playing in these parades, they're just playing the same old thing that some old, somebody has been jammed with on the street. The same thing I tell you, the bass player is playing the same three things on every nine numbers.
So you think they're not getting a good foundation?

No. No. No. Because they're also qualified and quality musician teachers, but there are enough of them that are not qualified, and they're not teaching, and they only go in there to get a check. And they don't give a damn how the kid turns out. Mm-hmm.
